REKA Brand Guidelines

The complete system behind REKA's identity — from what the brand stands for to every mark, colour, motif and application. AI for the physical world.
Version 1.0 · Maintained by REKA · holla@reka.re
01 · FOUNDATION

Foundation

↓ Export .md

Story

Origin

REKA began in 2013 as REKA Studios and became REKA Inisiatif in 2017. The name carries the Malay sense of to design, to invent. From the start the work has lived where software meets the physical world — vehicles, sensors, crowds, machines.

Today REKA is an applied-AI and automation R&D company, building autonomous systems and intelligence that operate in the real world, not just on screens.

Mission & values

The why
Enable people to create.

The mission is deliberately broad: REKA builds the tools, systems and intelligence that let people and organisations make things that move, sense and decide.

Start at the root

We begin at the root of the problem and build the answer to fit it, rather than forcing a fixed product onto it.

Honest engineering

We claim only what we can stand behind. No overstated results, no theatre.

Built for the real world

If it can't survive a road, a crowd or a factory floor, it isn't done.

Grounded, then global

Born on Southeast Asian roads, designed to operate anywhere.

Positioning

One line
AI for the physical world.

Supporting line: Born on Southeast Asian roads. Built for global operations. Use the primary line in product and marketing; the supporting line where heritage and reach matter.

Personality

How REKA feels

Five attributes that shape every expression of the brand and every product decision.

Precise

Every detail is intentional. If it serves no purpose, it has no place.

Inventive

New approaches to hard problems. Not familiar solutions repackaged.

Grounded

Honest about what works. No inflated claims, no theatre.

Forward

Building the next decade. Not catching up to the last one.

Quietly confident

The work speaks. The brand supports it.

The visual system reflects this: instrument-panel precision, technical detailing, orange used sparingly, and an engineered restraint throughout.

Proof

Heritage & credibility

System

Three forms

The logomark, the wordmark, and the full lockup. Use the lockup as the default; the mark alone where space is tight or the brand is already established; the wordmark where a mark would be redundant.

Wordmark
Lockup

Large-scale reference

The marks at display scale. Use these as the reference when placing the logo at large sizes on hero surfaces, merchandise, or signage.

Anatomy

Three forces

The mark is one disc holding three forces — Meniscus (Order), Scalpel (Discovery), Lightning (Chaos). Explode to see them; assemble to lock the mark back.

MeniscusOrder
ScalpelDiscovery
LightningChaos

Clear space

Exclusion zone

Keep clear space of at least X on every side, where X = the height of the logomark. Nothing — text, imagery, edges — intrudes into this zone.

XXXX

Minimum sizing

Legibility floor

Below these sizes the mark loses its detail. Digital is measured in pixels (mark height); print in millimetres.

24 px · mark · UI min
40 px · comfortable
22 px tall · lockup · screen min
≈ 16 mm wide · lockup · print min

Expressive variants

Dark surfaces

For splash screens, loaders and motion on near-black: the white HUD build, and the armour-panel Mecha build. Not for light backgrounds or formal documents.

REKA HUD

The mark rebuilt as instrument-panel fragments — orange accents, reticles and tech greebles. White build on near-black.

Color

Palette

Tap to copy

Orange is the signature; near-black is the home surface. Everything else is structure and text.

Usage

Proportion

Lead with near-black. Use surfaces for structure. Orange is an accent — a little goes a long way.

Near-black · 70%
Surfaces · 20%
Orange · 10%

Accessibility

Contrast (WCAG)

Computed contrast ratios for key pairings. Orange is an accent and headline colour on dark, not a body-text colour on light.

Aa

Ratios are AA at 4.5:1 (normal text) / 3:1 (large text); AAA at 7:1. Avoid orange text on white for anything small.

Type scale

A consistent scale keeps hierarchy clear across the system.

Usage

Rules
  • Poppins 600–700 for headings; 400 for body. Avoid weights below 400.
  • JetBrains Mono only for labels, figures, code and telemetry — uppercase, tracked ~0.08–0.14em.
  • Set body at 15–17px, line-height 1.55–1.6. Keep measure under ~70 characters.
  • Never substitute decorative or system fonts in brand materials.

Graphic language

Motifs

The vocabulary

REKA's visual language is a kit of HUD primitives — readout bars, hatches, brackets, panels, capsules and ticks — composed over a dot/grid texture. Reuse these, don't invent new ones.

Readout barsStacked ticks · data rhythm
HatchDiagonal rule fills
Bracket & slashFrame corners + cuts
PanelSolid angular slabs
CapsuleLozenge tags
TicksIndex markers

Stripes

Two systems

Two decorative stripes assembled from the motifs: a vertical rule for official documents, and a horizontal band for public surfaces.

Official document stripe · flush to the page edge

Motion

Principles

Motion is precise and purposeful, like an instrument powering on — never decorative jitter.

Boot, don't bounce

Elements power on: a quick scale/opacity reveal, then settle. Easing cubic-bezier(.2,.85,.2,1).

Calm ambient

Slow, continuous motion only (the HUD spins over ~46s). Nothing fast or looping tightly.

Reveal structure

Use explode/assemble to show how things are built; scan lines to show sensing.

Respect reduced-motion

All animation disables under prefers-reduced-motion.

08 · DIGITAL UI

Digital UI

↓ Export .md

Dashboard system

Auxiliary · Product UI

One design system, reskinned per product family. Layout, type, spacing and chamfer geometry are constant across all six products.

Design principles

Family-tinted dark sidebar
Each product family inherits its darkest palette shade as the sidebar background.
Rounded nav pills
8px border-radius. Active: white on 28% accent fill.
Slim branded topbar
Same dark as sidebar, 2px accent bottom-border. Page title + division label.
Four-corner chamfer cuts
KPI 7px · hero 12px · side panels 9px. No border-radius anywhere.
KPI cards with sparklines
Hero metric gets 2px accent top-border + 7-point sparkline.
Product-specific hero
Zone heatmap, unit grid, pipeline flow, dual-series trend, division matrix, product health.
Profile card at bottom
User avatar (accent-ringed), name + role above Settings.
Warm light surface
Public: #F7F6F3. Dark (Internal): #131318 + #1B1B24 cards.
